frozen_snapshot.english_definition: Showing active hostility or opposition towards someone.
frozen_snapshot.burmese_meaning: တစ်စုံတစ်ဦးအပေါ် ရန်လိုဆန့်ကျင်သည့် သဘောထားရှိသော
frozen_snapshot.example_sentence: His antagonistic remarks made cooperation between the teams harder.

publisher_observation.source_sense_summary: Formal adjective antagonistic to/towards somebody/something describes showing or feeling opposition. The original 'active hostility' is narrower and more negative than Oxford's full opposition sense; distinguish an unfriendly attitude from an ordinary disagreement.

unapproved_teaching_alternative.english_definition: Showing or feeling strong opposition to a person or idea, often in an unfriendly way.
unapproved_teaching_alternative.burmese_meaning: တစ်ဦးဦး သို့မဟုတ် အယူအဆတစ်ခုကို ပြင်းပြင်းထန်ထန် ဆန့်ကျင်ပြီး ရန်လိုသဘောထားပြသော
unapproved_teaching_alternative.example_sentence: The committee became antagonistic towards the proposed changes.

frozen_snapshot.english_definition: The quality of being based on personal choice rather than a fair rule.
frozen_snapshot.burmese_meaning: တရားမျှတသော စည်းမျဉ်းအစား ကိုယ်ပိုင်သဘောအတိုင်း ဆုံးဖြတ်ခြင်း၏ သဘောသဘာဝ
frozen_snapshot.example_sentence: Workers criticised the arbitrariness of the promotion decisions.

publisher_observation.source_sense_summary: Oxford marks the noun uncountable and separates lack of reason/system/plan (sometimes unfair) from unlimited exercise of power. Original 'personal choice rather than a fair rule' is too narrow and risks collapsing the two senses. Example about promotion decisions fits sense 1.

frozen_snapshot.english_definition: Showing steady and careful effort over a long period.
frozen_snapshot.burmese_meaning: အချိန်ကြာမြင့်စွာ ဇွဲရှိရှိနှင့် ဂရုတစိုက် ကြိုးစားလုပ်ဆောင်သော
frozen_snapshot.example_sentence: Her assiduous preparation helped the research team avoid errors.

publisher_observation.source_sense_summary: Formal adjective means working very hard and carefully. Long duration is not required by the Oxford definition; original 'over a long period' may add an unsupported restriction. Oxford Personal qualities c2 is a topic tag, not proof that this exact word is C2 or C1.

frozen_snapshot.english_definition: A feeling of emotional relief after expressing strong feelings.
frozen_snapshot.burmese_meaning: ပြင်းထန်သော ခံစားချက်များကို ဖော်ထုတ်ပြီးနောက် စိတ်ပေါ့ပါးသက်သာလာခြင်း
frozen_snapshot.example_sentence: Writing about the experience gave him a sense of catharsis.

publisher_observation.source_sense_summary: Oxford defines a process of releasing strong emotions to obtain relief, rather than merely the feeling of relief afterward. Noun is countable or uncountable, specialist; irregular plural catharses /kəˈθɑːsiːz/. Do not confuse with general relaxation or claim a CEFR badge.

frozen_snapshot.english_definition: To find a way around a rule, restriction or difficulty.
frozen_snapshot.burmese_meaning: စည်းကမ်း၊ ကန့်သတ်ချက် သို့မဟုတ် အခက်အခဲကို လှည့်ပတ်ကျော်လွှားသည်
frozen_snapshot.example_sentence: The company must not circumvent safety checks to save time.

publisher_observation.source_sense_summary: Oxford gives a transitive avoid-a-rule/difficulty sense and a distinct physically go-around-an-obstacle sense. Frozen example about safety checks fits first sense; avoid treating every circumvention as automatically illegal. Oxford Success c2 and Permission and obligation c2 are topic labels, not exact-sense CEFR ratings.

frozen_snapshot.english_definition: To join together to form one group or whole.
frozen_snapshot.burmese_meaning: အစုအဖွဲ့များ ပေါင်းစည်းပြီး တစ်စုတစ်စည်းတည်း ဖြစ်လာသည်
frozen_snapshot.example_sentence: Several small community groups began to coalesce around the proposal.

publisher_observation.source_sense_summary: Oxford marks coalesce intransitive; coalesce into something denotes several elements joining into a single group or whole. Frozen 'coalesce around the proposal' is plausible figurative use but preposition and meaning require independent usage checking; do not teach a transitive pattern 'coalesce something'.
